**Sarah Fredrika Sjöström** (Swedish: [[ˈsɑ̂ːra ˈɧø̂ːstrœm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Swedish "Help:IPA/Swedish")[swimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_\(sport\) "Swimming \(sport\)") specialising in the sprint [freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freestyle_swimming "Freestyle swimming") and [butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterfly_stroke "Butterfly stroke") events. She is one of the most decorated swimmers of all time.
As of 2024, Sjöström has won a total of [23 individual medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_World_Aquatics_Championships#Individual_events "Swimming at the World Aquatics Championships") at long course World Championships, more than any other swimmer in history. She was the first female swimmer to win five individual medals at a single [FINA World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA_World_Aquatics_Championships "FINA World Aquatics Championships"), a feat she accomplished in 2019. In 2021, Sjöström achieved a career total of over 1000 [most valuable player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_valuable_player "Most valuable player") points in the International Swimming League, becoming the first swimmer in history to do so. In 2022, she became the first swimmer from any country to have won a total of 28 medals at [LEN European Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LEN_European_Aquatics_Championships "LEN European Aquatics Championships"). She has won a total of 112 medals at [Swimming World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA_Swimming_World_Cup "FINA Swimming World Cup").
Sjöström is the current [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_swimming "List of world records in swimming") holder in the 50 metre butterfly ([long course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic-size_swimming_pool "Olympic-size swimming pool")). She is a former world record holder in the 50 metre freestyle (long course and [short course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_course_\(swimming\) "Short course \(swimming\)")), 100 metre butterfly (long course and short course), 100 metre freestyle (long course and short course), 200 metre freestyle (short course), and the 4×50 metre medley relay (short course). She is the first Swedish woman to win an [Olympic gold medal in swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the Summer Olympics").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-3) She won the [Overall Swimming World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA_Swimming_World_Cup "FINA Swimming World Cup") in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_FINA_Swimming_World_Cup "2017 FINA Swimming World Cup") and [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FINA_Swimming_World_Cup "2018 FINA Swimming World Cup"). In 2022, she became the first swimmer representing a country in Europe to win 10 individual World Championships gold medals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-CIIC26Jun2022-4)
Sjöström participated in five consecutive [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), from [Beijing 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics") through [Paris 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics"). She has won six Olympic medals: three gold (100 metre butterfly, 100 metre freestyle and 50 metre freestyle), two silver (200 metre freestyle and 50 metre freestyle), and one bronze (100 metre freestyle).
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]
### 2008–2009
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2008–2009")]
#### 2008 European Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2008 European Championships")]
On 22 March 2008, at the age of 14, Sjöström won the gold medal in the 100 metre [butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterfly_stroke "Butterfly stroke") at the [2008 European Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_European_Aquatics_Championships "2008 European Aquatics Championships") in [Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eindhoven "Eindhoven"), [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), with a time of 58.44 seconds.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-6) In the semi-finals the day before, she set a new [Swedish record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Swedish_records_in_swimming "List of Swedish records in swimming") of 58.38 seconds, breaking the previous record of 58.71 seconds by [Anna-Karin Kammerling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna-Karin_Kammerling "Anna-Karin Kammerling").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN21Mar2008-7) Three days earlier, she won her first medal of the Championships in the 4×100 metre freestyle relay, contributing a split time of 56.17 for the third leg of the relay in the preliminary heats before being substituted out for the finals relay and winning a bronze medal for her efforts when the finals relay placed third in 3:41.28.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN18Mar2008-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-TNYT18Mar2008-9) At the Swedish championships in 2008 in the same event, she finished in a time of 58.55 seconds.
#### 2008 Summer Olympics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2008 Summer Olympics")]
See also: [Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics")
Sjöström earned a spot on the [Swedish Swim Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Sweden at the 2008 Summer Olympics") for the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), China, where she finished 27th in the preliminary heats of the [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre butterfly") with a time of 59.08 and 29th in the preliminary heats of the [100 metre backstroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_backstroke "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre backstroke") with a time of 1:02.38, failing to advance to the semi-finals in both races. She also swam the backstroke leg of the [4×100 metre medley relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_medley_relay "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay") in the preliminaries, in which the Swedish team qualified in seventh place for the finals, though the team went on to be disqualified in the final for a false start. The day of the 4×100 metre medley relay final coincided with Sjöström's 15th birthday.

On 26 July 2009, at the [2009 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Aquatics_Championships "2009 World Aquatics Championships"), Sjöström set a [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_swimming#Women "List of world records in swimming") in the semifinals of the [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2009_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2009 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre butterfly") with a time of 56.44 seconds, surpassing [Inge de Bruijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inge_de_Bruijn "Inge de Bruijn")'s nine-year-old [record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_100_metres_butterfly#Long_course_2 "World record progression 100 metres butterfly").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Reuters26Jul2009-10) The next day, in the final of the event, she won the gold medal and improved her world record time to 56.06 seconds at just 15 years, 344 days of age.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Crouse27Jul2009-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Reuters27Jul2009-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-WR100fl2x2009July-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-15)
### 2010–2012
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2010–2012")]
#### 2010 European Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2010 European Championships")]
At the [2010 European Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_European_Aquatics_Championships "2010 European Aquatics Championships") in [Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest"), [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary "Hungary"), Sjöström defended her European title in the 100 metre butterfly by winning the event.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-16) With a split time of 53.77 seconds for the third leg of the 4×100 metre freestyle relay in the final, she helped Sweden win the bronze medal in a time of 3:38.81.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN9Aug2010-17) For the 4×100 metre medley relay, she anchored the relay in the final with a time of 53.73 seconds to help her country finish in 4:01.18 and win the silver medal.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN15Aug2010-18) In December 2011, she broke the Swedish record when she won the 100 metre freestyle at the Open Dutch Championships in Eindhoven. However, she failed to win a medal at the [2011 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_World_Aquatics_Championships "2011 World Aquatics Championships") in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-19)

#### 2012 European Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2012 European Championships")]
For Sjöström, 2012 was a year of both successes and setbacks. At the [2012 European Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_European_Aquatics_Championships "2012 European Aquatics Championships"), held in early summer in [Debrecen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debrecen "Debrecen"), Hungary, she achieved double gold medals in her individual events, with one in the 50 metre butterfly and one in the 100 metre freestyle.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-26) In her relay event, the 4×100 metre freestyle relay, she helped her team win the silver medal in a final time of 3:38.40, swimming the third leg of the relay in 54.04 seconds.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN21May2012-27)
#### 2012 Summer Olympics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2012 Summer Olympics")]
See also: [Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics")
At the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), Sjöström competed in four individual events,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-28) reaching the semi-finals of the [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle"), [100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre freestyle") and [200 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_200_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 200 metre freestyle"), and placing fourth in the final of the [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre butterfly") with a time of 57.17 seconds. Sjöström's world record was broken in this race by [Dana Vollmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Vollmer "Dana Vollmer") of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-29) In 2015, Sjöström regained the world record by improving it twice at the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Aquatics_Championships "2015 World Aquatics Championships"), held in [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-30)

On 29 July 2013, Sjöström won the gold medal in the [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2013_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2013 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre butterfly") at the [2013 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Aquatics_Championships "2013 World Aquatics Championships"), in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), with a time of 56.53 seconds, which was 0.44 seconds faster than silver medalist [Alicia Coutts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicia_Coutts "Alicia Coutts") of [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia") and 0.71 seconds faster than bronze medalist Dana Vollmer.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA29Jul2013f100fl-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Sejwal29Jul2013-32) Four days later, she won a silver medal in the 100 metre freestyle, finishing 0.55 seconds behind a first-time world champion in the event, [Cate Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cate_Campbell "Cate Campbell") of Australia, with a time of 52.89 seconds.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA2Aug2013f100fr-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-SBS3Aug2013-34)
#### 2013 European Short Course Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2013 European Short Course Championships")]
At the [2013 European Short Course Swimming Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_European_Short_Course_Swimming_Championships "2013 European Short Course Swimming Championships") in December in [Herning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herning "Herning"), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark"), Sjöström won four medals in individual events, a gold medal in the 50 metre butterfly with a [Championships record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_Championships_records_in_swimming "List of European Championships records in swimming") of 24.90 seconds, a gold medal in the 100 metre butterfly, a silver medal in the 50 metre freestyle, and a silver medal in the 100 metre freestyle, and two medals in relay events, one silver medal each in the 4×50 metre freestyle relay and 4×50 metre medley relay.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-35)
#### 2014 European Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2014 European Championships")]
On 5 July 2014, Sjöström broke the [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_50_metres_butterfly "World record progression 50 metres butterfly") in the [long course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_course "Long course") 50 metre butterfly, set at 25.07 by fellow Swedish swimmer [Therese Alshammar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Therese_Alshammar "Therese Alshammar") in 2009, with a time of 24.43 seconds. The margin of 0.64 seconds by which she lowered the world record compared to the prior record has been juxtaposed with [Bob Beamon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Beamon "Bob Beamon")'s 1968 long jump world record.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Lord5Jul2014-36) At the [2014 European Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_European_Aquatics_Championships "2014 European Aquatics Championships"), held in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") later that summer, she won three gold medals and four silver medals. On 18 August, she and her Swedish relay teammates won the gold medal in the 4×100 metre freestyle relay. The next day she also won the final of the 50 metre butterfly. On 20 August, the she won her third gold medal, this time in the 100 metre freestyle. She also won silver medals in the 4×200 metre freestyle relay, 100 metre butterfly, 50 metre freestyle and 4×100 metre medley relay.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-38)

In 2015, and leading up to the World Championships, Sjöström received the Jerring Prize and a [Victoria Scholarship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Scholarship "Victoria Scholarship").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-sarah-sjostrom-far-victoriastipendiet-2015-46) Approximately two months earlier, at the 2015 Eindhoven Swim Cup in April, she became the first female Swedish swimmer to achieve a time faster than 1:00.00 in the 100 metre backstroke, setting a new Swedish record with a personal best time of 59.98 seconds.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Keith5Apr2015-47) At the [2015 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Aquatics_Championships "2015 World Aquatics Championships"), held in July and August, she won a total of five medals, including gold medals in the [50 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre butterfly") and [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre butterfly") events, during the latter she broke the world record twice, first with a 55.74 in the semifinals then again with a 55.64 in the final.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-BBCS2Aug2015-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-yahoo_145243484-49) Her gold medal in the 50 metre butterfly was the first gold medal she won at a [FINA World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA_World_Aquatics_Championships "FINA World Aquatics Championships"). With both of the gold medals, she also became the first Swedish swimmer to win two World Championships gold medals during a single World Aquatics Championships. In the [100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre freestyle"), she won the silver medal with a time of 52.70 seconds, sharing the podium with Australian sisters [Bronte Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronte_Campbell "Bronte Campbell"), gold medalist, and Cate Campbell, bronze medalist.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA7Aug2015f100fr-50)
On the final day, Sjöström concluded competition with a bronze medal in the [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre freestyle") and a silver medal in the [4×100 metre medley relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_medley_relay "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay"). Thus she won medals in all four individual events, and in the three relay events there was a silver medal and two fourth-place finishes. In all, she won two gold medals, two silver medals and a bronze medal during world championship week; more medals than any Swede had previously won at the same world championships.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-yahoo_145243484-49)

split a 24.33 for the butterfly leg of the relay to help finish in a time of 1:45.34 and win the silver Before the end of the year, Sjöström was named as the first Swedish swimmer by _[Swimming World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_World "Swimming World")_ to receive their accolade "Swimmer of the Year in Europe"; she was also awarded the [Svenska Dagbladet Gold Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svenska_Dagbladet_Gold_Medal "Svenska Dagbladet Gold Medal"), an annual award "for the most significant Swedish sports achievement of the year", with the words "For explosive willpower, double world records and a historic gold cavalcade".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-sarah-sjostrom-far-victoriastipendiet-2015-46)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-yahoo_145243484-49)
#### 2016 European Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: 2016 European Championships")]
Ahead of her international competitions for the 2016 year, on 25 January 2016, Sjöström was awarded the Swedish public radio [Jerring Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerring_Award "Jerring Award") for the second year in a row.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-57) On the first day of swimming competition at the [2016 European Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_European_Aquatics_Championships "2016 European Aquatics Championships"), held in May in London, England, she won a bronze medal in the [4×100 metre freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_European_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2016 European Aquatics Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay"), leading-off the relay with a 53.48 to contribute to the final mark of 3:37.84.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN16May2016f4100fr-58) She followed up with a gold medal-win the next day in the [50 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_European_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2016 European Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre butterfly"), finishing first with a time of 24.99 seconds, which was 0.56 seconds slower than her world record time in the event.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN17May2016f50fl-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Brien17May2016-60) On the third day, she shared the podium with two Dutch swimmers in the [100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_European_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2016 European Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre freestyle"), winning the gold medal with a time of 52.82 seconds.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Marsteller18May2016-61) The fourth day, she won her final medal of the competition, a gold medal in the [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_European_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2016 European Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre butterfly") with a [Championships record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_Championships_records_in_swimming "List of European Championships records in swimming") time of 55.89 seconds.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN19May2016f100fl-62)
#### 2016 Summer Olympics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: 2016 Summer Olympics")]
See also: [Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics")
On 7 August 2016, Sjöström won the gold medal in the [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre butterfly") at the [2016 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"), setting a world record with a time of 55.48 seconds.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-SR8Aug2016-63) With her win she became the first female Swedish swimmer to win a gold medal at an [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-AFP8Aug2016-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Sse24Jan2023-65) She went on to win the silver medal in the [200 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_200_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 200 metre freestyle"), where she finished 0.35 seconds behind gold medalist [Katie Ledecky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Ledecky "Katie Ledecky") of the United States with a Swedish record time of 1:54.08, and the bronze medal in [100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre freestyle"), where she finished 0.29 seconds behind a two-way tie for the gold medal with a time of 52.99 seconds.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-WCBSTV9Aug2016-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-ESPN10Aug2016-67) With her medals, she became the second female swimmer in history and the fifth swimmer of any gender to win medals in the 100 metre freestyle, 200 metre freestyle, and the 100 metre butterfly at the same [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") or [long course World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the World Aquatics Championships"), after [Mark Spitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Spitz "Mark Spitz") ([1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1972_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 1972 Summer Olympics")), [Kornelia Ender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kornelia_Ender "Kornelia Ender") ([1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1975_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 1975 World Aquatics Championships"), [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1976_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 1976 Summer Olympics")), [Matt Biondi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Biondi "Matt Biondi") ([1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1986_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 1986 World Aquatics Championships"), [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1988_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 1988 Summer Olympics")) and [Michael Klim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Klim "Michael Klim") ([1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1998_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 1998 World Aquatics Championships")).[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-68)
### 2017–2019
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: 2017–2019")]
In January 2017, Sjöström competed at the 19th Luxembourg Euro Meet and won the 50 metre freestyle with a time of 24.01 seconds, the 100 metre freestyle with a 53.21, the 50 metre butterfly with a time of 25.02 seconds, and the 100 metre butterfly with a 57.12.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-69) Three months later, she competed in the Stockholm Swim Open and won the 50 metre butterfly with a time of 25.63 seconds.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-70) She also won the 100 metre butterfly with a time of 56.26 seconds.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-72) She also won the 50 metre freestyle, setting a time of 23.83 seconds, the second fastest time ever.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-73) In the 100 metre freestyle she took first-place with the time of 52.54 seconds, a new personal best and [Swedish record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Swedish_records_in_swimming "List of Swedish records in swimming").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-74)

event.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Zaccardi24Jul2017-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-TL25Jul2017-77) One day #### 2017 Swimming World Cup
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: 2017 Swimming World Cup")]
For the whole summer of 2017, Sjöström broke six world records in less than one month (the two at the aforementioned World Championships and later at [2017 Swimming World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_FINA_Swimming_World_Cup "2017 FINA Swimming World Cup") [short course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_course_\(swimming\) "Short course \(swimming\)") competitions in Moscow, 50 metre freestyle at 23.10 seconds and 100 metre freestyle at 50.77 seconds, and Eindhoven, 100 metre freestyle at 50.58 seconds and 200 metre freestyle at 1:50.43).[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Rieder2Aug2017-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA3Aug2017-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-WR100fr11Aug2017-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-WR200fr12Aug2017-91) As a simultaneous holder of eight world records on the short and long course, she became the swimmer to hold the most current world records in international swimming. In early August, Sjöström improved her time in the short course 50 metre freestyle, at races in Berlin, from 23.10 to 23.00.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-OT7Aug2017-92) In the race, however, she was second behind Ranomi Kromowidjojo, who with the time 22.93 took from Sjöström one of her eight records.

evening came in the 100 metre individual medley, finishing 0.95 seconds behind gold medalist [Katinka Hosszú](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katinka_Hossz%C3%BA "Katinka Hosszú") of Hungary in the [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN17Dec2017f100fl-96) She won her second gold medal approximately 48 minutes later, finishing first in the final of the 50 metre freestyle with a Championships record of 23.30 seconds.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN17Dec2017f50fr-97) Approximately 31 minutes later, she won her third and final gold medal of the night, splitting a At the [2019 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Aquatics_Championships "2019 World Aquatics Championships") held in [Gwangju](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwangju "Gwangju"), [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"), Sjöström won five medals, the most for a woman in individual events at the year's World Championships.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Ross28Jul2019-106) She won a gold medal in the [50 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2019_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2019 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre butterfly") with a time of 25.02 seconds, which marked the third consecutive gold medal she won in the event at the World Championships.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-107) In the [100 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2019_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2019 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre butterfly"), she won the silver medal with a time of 56.22 seconds to finish less than four-tenths of a second behind gold medalist [Maggie Mac Neil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maggie_Mac_Neil "Maggie Mac Neil") of [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-YS22Jul2019-108) She won her second silver medal of the Championships in the [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2019_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2019 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre freestyle"), where she finished 0.02 seconds behind first-place finisher Simone Manuel with a time of 24.07 seconds.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-TAP28Jul2019-109) For her first bronze medal, she placed third in the [200 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2019_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_200_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2019 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 200 metre freestyle") with a time of 1:54.78, finishing within six-tenths of a second of gold medalist Federica Pellegrini and within two-tenths of a second of silver medalist [Ariarne Titmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariarne_Titmus "Ariarne Titmus") of Australia.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA24Jul2019-110) In the [100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2019_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2019 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre freestyle") she won her second of two bronze medals with a time of 52.46 seconds, sharing the podium with Simone Manuel, gold medalist, and Cate Campbell, silver medalist.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA26Jul2019-111)
Based on her performances and result as the most decorated female competitor in individual events at the Championships, Sjöström was named FINA female swimmer of the meet, which she also won in 2017.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Ross28Jul2019-106)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-112)
#### 2019 International Swimming League
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: 2019 International Swimming League")]
In the fall of 2019, she was a member of the [inaugural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_International_Swimming_League "2019 International Swimming League") [International Swimming League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Swimming_League "International Swimming League") competing for the [Energy Standard Swim Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_Standard_Swim_Club "Energy Standard Swim Club") of which she was co-captain with [Chad le Clos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_le_Clos "Chad le Clos"). The team won the overall title in the season finale in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), United States, in December.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-113) At the first stop of the regular season, in [Indianapolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis"), United States, she won the Most Valuable Player title, amassing 55.5 points over the competition, and after the season finale in Las Vegas, she was named the overall Most Valuable Player for the entire season with 243.5 points. During the season, she won the 50 metre freestyle in three matches, the 100 metre freestyle in two matches, the 50 metre butterfly in three matches, and the 100 metre butterfly in one match. She also won the 50 metre freestyle skins event at three matches.
### 2020–2021
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: 2020–2021")]
#### 2020 International Swimming League
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: 2020 International Swimming League")]
In the [2020 International Swimming League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_International_Swimming_League "2020 International Swimming League") season Sjöström placed 5th overall in points in 2020, due in part to a back injury that made her sit out of a full match.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-114) She ranked second to [Caeleb Dressel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caeleb_Dressel "Caeleb Dressel") in points-per-match with 59.4, noted 16 individual wins, including three in the skins.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-:0-115) And while neither were official world records, Sjöström also featured on Energy Standard's women's and mixed 4×100 freestyle relays that were both the fastest of all time.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-:0-115)
#### 2020 Summer Olympics

See also: [Swimming at the 2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2020 Summer Olympics")
Due to a broken elbow Sjöström accidentally obtained by falling on ice in February 2020, she did not compete at the [2020 European Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_European_Aquatics_Championships "2020 European Aquatics Championships").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Dampf28Jun2021-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Baldwin1Aug2021-117) Olympics").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Baldwin1Aug2021-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-118) In the [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle") at the 2020 Olympic Games in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan, and held in 2021 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), and winning a medal at the Olympic Games earned her the "Olympic Resilience Award" for the 2020 Summer Olympics from _[Swimming World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_World "Swimming World")_.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Rieder14Sep2021-119) In her other events, Sjöström placed fifth in the [100 metre #### 2021 European Short Course Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: 2021 European Short Course Championships")]
At the [2021 European Short Course Swimming Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_European_Short_Course_Swimming_Championships "2021 European Short Course Swimming Championships") held at the [Palace of Water Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Water_Sports "Palace of Water Sports") in [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan"), Russia in November, Sjöström competed in nine events, winning four gold medals, one each in the 50 metre freestyle, 100 metre freestyle, 50 metre butterfly, and 100 metre butterfly, a silver medal in the 4×50 metre medley relay, and a bronze medal in the 100 metre individual medley as well as placing fourth in the 4×50 metre mixed medley relay and the 4×50 metre mixed freestyle relay and fifth in the 4×50 metre freestyle relay.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LEN7Nov2021cr-121)
#### 2021 International Swimming League
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: 2021 International Swimming League")]
In the [2021 International Swimming League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_International_Swimming_League "2021 International Swimming League"), Sjöström became the first swimmer in history, male or female, to achieve over 1000 [most valuable player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_valuable_player "Most valuable player") points as part of their time competing in the International Swimming League, out-ranking the second-ranked Caeleb Dressel by over 50 points.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Keith13December2021-122) Sjöström won most valuable player honors both for the entire 2021 season and for the 2021 final match.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-D'Addona4Dec2021-123) For the whole 2021 season, Sjöström was the top-earning athlete, winning $269,125 in the form of prize money, which was over $70,000 more than the next-highest-earning athlete [Siobhán Haughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siobh%C3%A1n_Haughey "Siobhán Haughey").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Keith5Dec2021-124)

In the morning of day three, Sjöström qualified for the semifinals of the [50 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_\(25_m\)_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_butterfly "2021 FINA World Swimming Championships \(25 m\) – Women's 50 metre butterfly") ranking first with a time of 24.92 seconds.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA18Dec2021h50fl-133) Sjöström won the silver medal in the final of the 100 metre freestyle later in the day with a time of 51.31, finishing less than four-tenths of a second behind gold medalist [Siobhán Haughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siobh%C3%A1n_Haughey "Siobhán Haughey") of [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA18Dec2021f100fr-134) For the semifinals of the 50 metre butterfly, she qualified for the final ranking second with a 24.94.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA18Dec2021sf50fl-135) In the final the following day, Sjöström won the silver medal with a time of 24.51 seconds.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA19Dec2021f50fl-136) The fifth morning, Sjöström advanced to the semifinals of the [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_\(25_m\)_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "2021 FINA World Swimming Championships \(25 m\) – Women's 50 metre freestyle") ranking first by over three-tenths of a second with a 23.31 in the prelims heats.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA20Dec2021h50fr-137) In the semifinals she swam one-hundredth of a second faster, qualifying for the final with a time of 23.30 seconds.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA20Dec2021sf50fr-138)
On the sixth and final day, Sjöström led-off the [4×50 metre freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_\(25_m\)_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_50_metre_freestyle_relay "2021 FINA World Swimming Championships \(25 m\) – Women's 4 × 50 metre freestyle relay") with a 23.50 in the prelims, helping qualify the relay to the final ranking third.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA21Dec2021h450fr-139) In her first final of the evening, Sjöström helped set a new [Swedish record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Swedish_records_in_swimming "List of Swedish records in swimming") of 1:34.54 and win the silver medal in the 4×50 metre freestyle relay with a lead-off split of 23.33 seconds.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA21Dec2021f450fr-140) For her next race, the 50 metre freestyle final, Sjöström won the gold medal and set a new [Championships record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Championships_records_in_swimming "List of World Championships records in swimming") of 23.08 seconds, breaking the former record of 23.19 set by [Ranomi Kromowidjojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranomi_Kromowidjojo "Ranomi Kromowidjojo") of the Netherlands in 2018 by over one-tenth of a second.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA21Dec2021f50fr-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Sutherland21Dec2021-142) In her final event of the championships, Sjöström split a 54.65 for the butterfly leg of the [4×100 metre medley relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_\(25_m\)_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_medley_relay "2021 FINA World Swimming Championships \(25 m\) – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay"), helping win the gold medal in a new [European record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_records_in_swimming "List of European records in swimming") time of 3:46.20.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-FINA21Dec2021f4100mr-143)
At the end of 2021, Sjöström was the only swimmer to rank in the top ten internationally in two or more individual long course metre events for 11 or more consecutive years, 2021 inclusive, ranking in the top ten in the 100 metre freestyle for 12 years and the 50 metre butterfly and 100 metre butterfly for 13 years.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Takata3Jan2022-144) Additionally, Sjöström was tied with Katie Ledecky for number two in terms of total number of individual world records set in the 21st century, each having achieved 14 individual world records, and was six world records behind number one ranked [Katinka Hosszú](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katinka_Hossz%C3%BA "Katinka Hosszú").[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Takata14Jan2022-145)

### 2023
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: 2023")]
At the 2023 Stockholm Swim Open in April, Sjöström won the long course 50 metre freestyle with the fastest time in the world for the 2023 year by a female at that point in the time, a [2023 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Aquatics_Championships "2023 World Aquatics Championships") qualifying time of 23.92 seconds.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-LT15Apr2023-174)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-Nuoto15Apr2023-175)
At the [2023 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Aquatics_Championships "2023 World Aquatics Championships"), Sjöström won the long course [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2023_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre freestyle"), breaking her own [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_50_metres_freestyle "World record progression 50 metres freestyle") in the semifinal. In doing so, she set the record for the longest period of time in between world-record setting performances by an individual swimmer, 14 years and 3 days after first breaking the [100 metre butterfly world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_100_metres_butterfly "World record progression 100 metres butterfly") in 2009.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-176) She also won the [50 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2023_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 100 metre butterfly") for the fifth time in a row at the World Aquatic Championships. These two medals led her to tie and then overtake [Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps") as the swimmer with the most individual World Aquatic Championship medals at 21 in her career.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-177) She additionally performed on Sweden's [400 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2023_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay") and [400 metre medley relays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2023_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_medley_relay "Swimming at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay"); notably, her lead-off split of 52.24 in finals for the freestyle relay would have earned her a silver medal in the 100 metre freestyle.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-178)
### 2024
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: 2024")]
#### 2024 World Championships
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: 2024 World Championships")]
At the [2024 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Aquatics_Championships "2024 World Aquatics Championships") in Doha, Sjöström won the long course [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2024 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre freestyle") as well as the [50 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_World_Aquatics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2024 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre butterfly"). The latter for a sixth time in a row at the World Aquatic Championships.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-179)
#### 2024 Olympic Games
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: 2024 Olympic Games")]
Sjöström, now focusing on the shortest distances, had only planned to swim [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle") at the [Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"). However, she decided to join [100 m freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre freestyle") as it suited her schedule between the [4×100m freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay") and the 50 metre freestyle.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-180) She first raced in the heats and the final of the [4x100m freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay"), where the Swedish team finished 5th in the final setting a new national record.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-181) She then went on to win the gold in 100 metre freestyle on 31 July with a time of 52.16 seconds. Despite being the World Record holder, Sjöström had never won a gold medal in this distance at the global level.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-182) On the last day of competition she won another gold medal in the [50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle"), with a time of 23.71 seconds.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m#cite_note-183) She closed her Olympic Games with a 7th place finish in the [4x100m medley relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_4_%C3%97_100_metre_medley_relay "Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay") alongside her Swedish teammates.

## Accomplishments and awards
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sarah_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m&action=edit&section=51 "Edit section: Accomplishments and awards")]
Sjöström won the gold in the 100 m freestyle at the 2024 Paris Olympics. She won the gold medal in the 100 m butterfly at the 2016 Rio Summer Olympics on 7 August 2016, setting an Olympic and World record with a time of 55.48. She also won a gold medal in 100 m butterfly in the World Championships in Rome 2009 and set the world record.
